[[Category:Cosmology]]
The '''cosmological fluid''' is a large-scale model of the [[Universe]]'s content.

It applies [[the Cosmological Principle]] and describes the Universe on large scales as a perfect fluid of '''energy density''' $\rho(t)$ and pressure $p(t)$.

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

== Three species ==

{{#content:Q2620}}

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Species
! Content
! $p,\rho$
! $\rho,a$
|-
| Non-relativistic matter
| Galaxies, baryons, and cold dark matter
| $p_M=0$
| $\rho_M\propto a^{-3}$
|-
| Radiation
| Photons and ultra-relativistic particles 
| $p_R=\rho_R/3$
| $\rho_R\propto a^{-4}$
|-
| Vacuum energy
| 
| $p_\Lambda=-\rho_\Lambda$
| $\rho_\Lambda=\text{constant}$
|}

{{Hidden proof}}
Example proof for the radiation case, other two cases are similar:

$$
\rho_R(t)=\frac{\rho_R(t)}{3}.
$$

Substituting this into the continuity equation,

$$
\dot{\rho}_R(t)
=
-3\frac{\dot{a}(t)}{a(t)}
\left(\rho_R(t)+\frac{\rho_R(t)}{3}\right)
=
-4\frac{\dot{a}(t)}{a(t)}\rho_R(t).
$$

Dividing by $\rho_R(t)$ for $\rho_R(t)>0$,

$$
\frac{\dot{\rho}_R(t)}{\rho_R(t)}
=
-4\frac{\dot{a}(t)}{a(t)}.
$$

Since

$$
\frac{\dot{\rho}_R(t)}{\rho_R(t)}
=
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\ln\rho_R(t),
\qquad
\frac{\dot{a}(t)}{a(t)}
=
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\ln a(t),
$$

integrating with respect to $t$ yields

$$
\ln\rho_R(t)=-4\ln a(t)+C.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\rho_R(t)=e^C a(t)^{-4}\propto a^{-4}.
$$
{{End hidden}}

== Aggregation ==
Since each component is independent,

$$
\rho_\text{total}(t)=\sum \rho(t),\, 
p_\text{total}(t)=\sum_x p(t).
$$

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
